pages.title: Menus
pages.content:
MENUS

Menus

Lunch runs Tuesday to Friday and dinner Tuesday to Saturday. Every price is in euros, and the list below is the whole offer.

Lunch, Tuesday to Friday

Lunch is served Tuesday to Friday from 11:30 to 14:30. The last order is at 13:45, and the sitting runs about 75 minutes, so two or three courses finish before the room turns toward the break. Two courses are €26. Three courses are €32. The list is short and follows the Tuesday delivery from Polder Vegetable Co-op, which is why the vegetables move while the prices stay put. A vegetarian version of either lunch menu is the same price.

Three plates from recent lunch services, as examples of the week rather than a fixed carte: a spring vegetable starter on stoneware; a vegetable plate with bread baked that morning from stone-milled flour; and a pear tart with cream. On Wednesday and Friday, when Harbour Day Boats has delivered, the main plate may be roast fish with white beans and greens. Allergens are noted on request at the table. Lea Fischer leads the lunch service.

LUNCH

Lunch, two courses

Spring vegetable starter · vegetable plate with fresh bread · pear tart with cream

€26

Lunch, three courses

Roast fish with white beans and greens on Wednesday and Friday

€32

Dinner, Tuesday to Saturday

Dinner is served Tuesday to Saturday from 17:30 to 22:30. The last seating is at 21:00. Early dinner seatings run from 17:30 to 18:30, and the table is yours for two hours. Late dinner seatings run from 20:00 to 21:00, and the table is yours until close. The dinner menu is four courses at €58. The kitchen tasting is six courses at €78. A wine pairing of four glasses is €38 with the dinner menu. The vegetarian version of either menu is the same price.

Three plates from recent dinner services, written as examples: the spring vegetable starter from the Tuesday crates; roast fish with white beans and greens on the evenings the boats have delivered; and, to finish, hard cheese with oat crackers or the pear tart with cream. Elena Vasquez writes the list after the crates are unpacked, and the pass cooks what is on it. The same menus, at the same prices, go to the private room when a group has booked it.

DINNER

Dinner menu, four courses

Spring vegetable starter · roast fish with white beans and greens · hard cheese with oat crackers

€58

Kitchen tasting, six courses

The whole list from the pass, vegetarian version at the same price

€78

Wine pairing, four glasses

Poured with the dinner menu, grape and region named with each glass

€38

Children and diets

A children's plate, for guests under 12, is €14. It can be ordered at lunch or at dinner and comes from the same pass as the adult menus. Every menu has a vegetarian version at the same price as the menu it follows: €26 or €32 at lunch, €58 or €78 at dinner. Tell us when you book, or tell the host when you arrive, and the kitchen will cook that version. Allergens are noted on request. Before the first plate, the kitchen will walk the list with you from the menu Elena has written for that week.

House-made drinks without alcohol can be poured with each course on request. That line lives with the wine list and has no price of its own. The six published prices are the full list: the two lunch menus, the dinner menu, the kitchen tasting, the wine pairing, and the children's plate. No other amount is added at the table.

CHILDREN

Children's plate

For guests under 12, lunch or dinner, from the same pass

€14

Who grows the food →

pages.title: Reservations
pages.content:
RESERVE

Reservations

Tables open thirty days ahead. Choose a sitting, then book online or call +31 10 555 0142.

Three ways to sit down

Weekday lunch is Tuesday to Friday, 11:30 to 14:30, and the sitting is about 75 minutes. Last order is at 13:45. It is the service for two courses at €26 or three courses at €32. Early dinner is Tuesday to Saturday, with seatings from 17:30 to 18:30, and the table is yours for two hours. Late dinner is Tuesday to Saturday as well, with seatings from 20:00 to 21:00. That 21:00 seating is the last of the night, and the table is yours until close at 22:30.

The room seats 40 people: 32 at tables and 8 at the counter. The booking form takes parties of 1 to 6. If you are walking past at the start of service, you may ask for a counter seat. Groups of 7 to 12 use the private room, which seats 12 and asks for a minimum of 8. The restaurant is closed on Sunday and Monday.

Weekday lunch

Tue–Fri · 11:30–14:30 · about 75 minutes

Book this sitting →

Early dinner

Tue–Sat · 17:30–18:30 · table for 2 hours

Book this sitting →

Late dinner

Tue–Sat · 20:00–21:00 · until close

Book this sitting →

Four steps to a table

The booking has four steps. First, choose a sitting: weekday lunch, early dinner, or late dinner. The times above are the seatings we take. Second, book online or call +31 10 555 0142. The form asks for your name, your email, the date, the time, and the number of guests, from 1 to 6. You may also write to table@shokutaku.example. Mateo Rossi looks after reservations. Third, wait for the email confirmation, and for the reminder that arrives the day before.

Check the date, the sitting, and the size of the party while there is still time to write back. Fourth, arrive for the time you booked. The table is held for 15 minutes. There is no deposit. A party of 7 to 12 does not use this form. That party is booked as private dining, by email to the same address, with Mateo.

  1. Choose a sitting. Weekday lunch, early dinner or late dinner.
  2. Book online or call. +31 10 555 0142, or table@shokutaku.example.
  3. Email confirmation. A reminder arrives the day before.
  4. Arrive. The table is held for 15 minutes. No deposit.

How far ahead can I book a table?

Tables open 30 days ahead. That window is the diary. When you need a date further out, call or write and Mateo Rossi will tell you when that morning's bookings open. A confirmed table is held for 15 minutes past the time you booked. Cancel by phone or by email at least 24 hours ahead, on +31 10 555 0142 or at table@shokutaku.example. The same address sends the confirmation and the reminder the day before. Parties of 1 to 6 book a table in the main room, at one of the 32 table seats or, when you ask on arrival, at one of the 8 counter seats.

Parties of 7 to 12 are seated in the private room. That room holds 12 and needs at least 8, on the dinner menu at €58 per guest or the kitchen tasting at €78 per guest. There is no deposit on a dining-room table or on a private booking.

BOOK

Request a table

Tables open thirty days ahead and are held for fifteen minutes. The form opens an email to the restaurant; Mateo Rossi confirms by email and sends a reminder the day before.

Parties of 7 to 12 are booked as private dining.

When are you open?

Lunch is Tuesday to Friday, 11:30 to 14:30, and the last order is at 13:45. Dinner is Tuesday to Saturday, 17:30 to 22:30, and the last seating is at 21:00. Sunday and Monday the restaurant is closed, and the private room is closed with it. Early dinner seatings are 17:30 to 18:30, with the table for two hours. Late dinner seatings are 20:00 to 21:00, with the table until close. A weekday lunch sitting is about 75 minutes.

Those hours are the hours on the booking form. The kitchen week begins with the Tuesday vegetable delivery, which is the first lunch of the new menu, and it ends on Saturday night. Bread is shaped on the mornings we are open. If you are choosing between sittings, the difference is time at the table, not a different price list: lunch is €26 or €32, and dinner is €58 or €78, whenever you sit inside those hours.

pages.title: Private dining
pages.content:
PRIVATE

Private dining

The private room seats 12 guests, with a minimum of 8. Dinner uses the same menus and the same euro prices as the dining room.

A long table for twelve

The private room is a long oak table set for twelve, with linen, in daylight before anyone arrives. It is where we seat groups of 7 to 12. Twelve is the maximum and eight is the minimum, so one menu can leave the pass for the whole table. Elena Vasquez cooks the dinner the dining room is eating that night. The kitchen does not write a separate private carte. Tomasz Nowak hosts on the floor, and Mateo Rossi arranges the date, the guest count, and the menu before the evening.

Bread from Jonas Berg's morning bake is on the table, the same loaves as in the dining room. The main room's 32 table seats and 8 counter seats stay on their own bookings. This room is the extra twelve, in the same building at Havenstraat 41, and it shares the open kitchen.

Menus and prices

The dinner menu is four courses at €58 per guest. The kitchen tasting is six courses at €78 per guest. These are the dining-room prices, with no extra amount for the private room. A vegetarian version of either menu is the same price per guest. Wine pairing is €38 per guest, four glasses, poured with the dinner menu. Wines by the glass are named by grape and region on the wine page, and they carry no separate private-room price.

House-made non-alcoholic drinks can be poured with each course on request, and that request has no listed price. A children's plate, for a guest under 12, is €14. Allergens are noted on request when the menu is confirmed. The menus are the dinner menu and the kitchen tasting, served on dinner hours, Tuesday to Saturday, from 17:30 to 22:30, with the last seating at 21:00.

PER GUEST

Dinner menu, four courses

Served on dinner hours, Tuesday to Saturday

€58

Kitchen tasting, six courses

Vegetarian version at the same price

€78

Wine pairing, four glasses

Optional, poured with the dinner menu

€38

Enquire, then confirm, then dinner

Write to table@shokutaku.example with the date, the number of guests, and whether you want the dinner menu at €58 or the tasting at €78. Call +31 10 555 0142 if you would rather speak to Mateo Rossi. The main-room form stops at 6 guests. A party of 7 to 12 belongs in this room. The path has four beats. Enquire, by email or by phone. Then a menu call, when Mateo or Elena walks through the four-course menu or the six-course tasting, the wine pairing at €38, and any allergens.

Then confirm the date and the headcount, between 8 and 12, and the menu. Then dinner at the long table. Enquire inside the same 30-day window as the dining room. Cancel by phone or email at least 24 hours ahead. There is no deposit. Confirmation arrives by email, with a reminder the day before.

  1. Enquire by email or phone.
  2. Menu call with Mateo or Elena.
  3. Confirm the date, 8 to 12 guests and the menu.
  4. Dinner at the long table.

pages.title: The room
pages.content:
ROOM

The room

Shokutaku Dining opened in 2014 in a former bakery at Havenstraat 41, Rotterdam. Elena Vasquez cooks at the open pass, and Tomasz Nowak hosts the room.

Opened in 2014, in a former bakery

In 2014 Elena Vasquez and Tomasz Nowak opened Shokutaku Dining at Havenstraat 41, 3024 Rotterdam, the Netherlands. The address had been a bakery. What remains of that work is practical: Jonas Berg shapes loaves on a floured bench at dawn, and the flour arrives weekly from Molen Ten Wind, already stone-milled. The dining room took the place of the bakery counter. Forty seats is the size they kept. It is small enough for one pass to cook for the whole room, and close enough to the street for lunch to be a weekday habit.

Elena is chef-owner. Tomasz is co-owner and host. She is at the pass. He is on the floor. The short menu was the plan from the opening year, written from what comes to the back door rather than from a long standing carte.

The open pass

The kitchen sits in the middle of the room. It is open, with a steel pass and white plates stacked within reach. Thirty-two seats are at oak tables. Eight seats are at the counter, where the plating is in plain view. Forty is the whole dining room. The private room, for 8 to 12 guests, is separate and eats the same food. Elena plates at the pass: a herb on a white plate, the sauce kept small, the dish walked a few steps to the table.

Amara Mensah, the sous chef, keeps mise en place on the steel bench with the kitchen team. In the evening the oak and the pale plaster are the same, with low lamps and the kitchen still lit at the back. Counter and tables share one menu. The price does not change with the seat.

THE PASS

Forty seats around one open kitchen.

The weekday lunch idea

Lunch is the meal the hours were built around. Tuesday to Friday, 11:30 to 14:30, about 75 minutes, last order at 13:45. Two courses are €26 and three courses are €32. Lea Fischer leads that service. The menu for the week is written after the Tuesday delivery from Polder Vegetable Co-op. Fish from Harbour Day Boats arrives on Wednesday and Friday, so roast fish with white beans and greens is a lunch plate on those days and a dinner plate the same evenings.

Dinner runs Tuesday to Saturday, 17:30 to 22:30, last seating 21:00, at €58 for four courses or €78 for the six-course tasting. Sunday and Monday the room is closed. A neighbourhood lunch holds if the price is plain and the sitting has a clear end. Both are printed, and both are the ones we book.

Bread at six

Jonas Berg starts the bread while Havenstraat is still quiet. He shapes loaves on a floured bench, using the weekly flour from Molen Ten Wind. By the time the tables are set, the bread for lunch is cooling. The same bake goes to dinner and to the long table when the private room is in use. The pear tart with cream is his on the days it is on the list. Pastry follows the fruit the Tuesday crates brought, so the tart appears in the weeks the fruit is there.

When it is on, it closes lunch and dinner as the sweet course. The story we tell about the old bakery stays narrow on purpose. A bench, a weekly delivery of stone-milled flour, and bread on the table at the start of service: that is the part of 2014 the room still uses every day we are open.

The three growers →

Seven people →

Elena Vasquez and Tomasz Nowak

Chef-owner · Co-owner and host

Elena Vasquez is chef-owner. She opened Shokutaku Dining in 2014 with Tomasz Nowak and cooks at the open pass in the middle of the room. She writes the short menu after the Tuesday delivery and plates lunch and dinner for the forty seats, and for the private table when a group has booked it. Tomasz Nowak is co-owner and host. He seats the room, keeps lunch and dinner moving across 32 table seats and 8 counter seats, and is the person you meet when you arrive for a sitting.

The two of them still split the service the way they did at opening: she on the pass, he on the floor, in the same building on Havenstraat. Questions about a booking go to Mateo. Questions about the plate in front of you can come to either of them.

Amara Mensah, Jonas Berg, and Priya Raman

Sous chef · Bread and pastry · Wine and drinks

Amara Mensah is sous chef. She runs mise en place on the steel bench and cooks the line with Elena through lunch and dinner. The herbs, the beans, the greens from Tuesday's crates, and the fish on Wednesday and Friday all pass through her station before they reach the pass. Jonas Berg is bread and pastry. He shapes the loaves at dawn from stone-milled flour delivered weekly by Molen Ten Wind, and he bakes the pear tart with cream in the weeks the fruit is in the crates.

The bread is on every table, including the long table for twelve. Priya Raman is wine and drinks. She pours by the glass, naming grape and region, and she pours the four-glass pairing at €38 with the dinner menu. House-made non-alcoholic drinks, on request with each course, are hers as well.

Mateo Rossi and Lea Fischer

Reservations and private dining · Lunch service lead

Mateo Rossi looks after reservations and private dining. He takes parties of 1 to 6 through the form, the phone at +31 10 555 0142, and table@shokutaku.example. He sends the email confirmation and the reminder the day before, holds each table for 15 minutes, and takes cancellations made at least 24 hours ahead. Groups of 7 to 12 come to him for the private room: enquire, menu call, confirm, then dinner, at €58 or €78 per guest.

The diary opens 30 days ahead. There is no deposit. Lea Fischer is lunch service lead. Tuesday to Friday, from 11:30 to 14:30, she runs the 75-minute sitting, the last order at 13:45, and the two lunch prices, €26 and €32. Seven people, one pass, one floor.

pages.title: Growers
pages.content:
GROWERS

Growers

Three producers supply the kitchen. Vegetables come on Tuesday, flour weekly, and fish on Wednesday and Friday.

The Tuesday delivery

The menu changes with the Tuesday delivery. Crates of vegetables arrive at the back door in the early light, Polder Vegetable Co-op unloads them, and Elena Vasquez writes the week's list from what is in the crates. Tuesday lunch is the first service to cook them. Dinner the same night follows the same list. The writing then carries the room through Saturday, with fish added on Wednesday and Friday when Harbour Day Boats delivers.

Roots, greens, and the fruit that decides the pear tart all come through that door. Flour does not: Molen Ten Wind brings stone-milled flour on its own weekly delivery, for Jonas Berg's bread. The restaurant keeps a short menu because the crates are the menu. Lunch at €26 or €32 and dinner at €58 or €78 are built on that delivery, and the vegetarian version of each menu stays at the same price.

Polder Vegetable Co-op

Vegetables · Tuesday

Polder Vegetable Co-op brings the vegetables, and the day is Tuesday. The crates are unloaded at the back door before lunch. From them come the spring vegetable starter, the greens beside the roast fish, and the fruit for pastry when the week supplies it. Elena builds both lunch menus and both dinner menus around that delivery. Two courses at lunch are €26 and three are €32. Four courses at dinner are €58 and the six-course tasting is €78.

A vegetarian version of each one uses the same price, because the vegetables are already the centre of the list. The co-op supplies vegetables only. Fish and flour move on other days, from the other two producers. Tuesday is the first day the dining room is open in the week, and it is open because the crates are here. Sunday and Monday stay closed, and the next list waits for the next Tuesday.

Molen Ten Wind

Stone-milled flour · weekly

Molen Ten Wind supplies stone-milled flour, and the delivery is weekly. Jonas Berg uses it for the loaves he shapes at dawn and for the pastry, including the pear tart with cream when pears are among the Tuesday fruit. The bread is on the table at weekday lunch, at dinner from Tuesday to Saturday, and on the long oak table when the private room is booked for 8 to 12 guests. It is not a course with a price of its own.

It sits inside the menus already published: €26 or €32 at lunch, €58 or €78 at dinner. One morning bake is the bake for that day. The loaves torn over linen at the first seating are from the same bench as the bread at the late seating, which ends with the last table at 21:00 and close at 22:30. The mill is the second of the three producers, between the vegetable co-op and the boats.

Harbour Day Boats

Fish · Wednesday and Friday

Harbour Day Boats brings the fish on Wednesday and Friday. Those are the days the roast fish with white beans and greens is on the pass, at lunch and again at dinner. The beans and the greens are from Tuesday's vegetable crates. The fish is the midweek delivery that gives the list its main plate on those two days. The kitchen cooks that fish inside the ordinary menus. Lunch remains €26 for two courses or €32 for three. Dinner remains €58 for four courses or €78 for six.

There is no extra line for fish on the price list. The boats are the third producer. With the co-op and the mill, the week has a plain shape: vegetables on Tuesday, flour on its weekly drop, fish on Wednesday and Friday, bread every morning we are open, and a dark kitchen on Sunday and Monday. Book the sitting, and the delivery days tell you what the pass is cooking.

pages.title: Wine and drinks
pages.content:
WINE

Wine and drinks

Priya Raman pours the wine and the house-made drinks. The pairing has one price. Wines by the glass are listed by grape and region only.

By the glass

Six wines are poured by the glass. Each line names the grape and the region only. Priya Raman keeps the six and will tell you which bottles are open when you sit down. Chenin Blanc, Loire. Riesling, Mosel. Albariño, Rías Baixas. Gamay, Beaujolais. Pinot Noir, Burgundy. Sangiovese, Tuscany. A glass may be ordered at lunch or at dinner, at a table, at one of the eight counter seats, or with a private dinner. The list is the same in each place.

If you want the kitchen's sequence instead of a single glass, take the pairing: four glasses with the dinner menu. The by-the-glass lines stay free of prices, vintages, and producer names, so the choice at the table is the grape and the place it was grown. Priya says those two things again as she pours. Allergens in a dish are a kitchen question. What is in the glass is hers to answer.

Wine pairing, four glasses

The wine pairing is €38. It is four glasses, poured with the dinner menu. The dinner menu is four courses at €58, and the kitchen tasting is six courses at €78. The pairing has one price per guest, in the dining room and at the private table. Priya Raman pours it in the order of the courses. She names the grape and the region as each glass arrives, in the same plain form as the list above. Add the pairing when you book, or ask before the first course.

For a private dinner, add it on the menu call so the glasses are counted for every guest, and the room is booked for 8 to 12. The pairing is optional. Both dinner menus are served without it. Lunch keeps its own prices, €26 and €32, and a lunch guest who wants wine orders by the glass from the six lines. The €38 pairing belongs to dinner.

Wine pairing, four glasses

With the dinner menu, one price per guest, dining room and private table

€38

House-made drinks with the courses

House-made non-alcoholic drinks are poured with each course on request. There is no price on that line. Ask Priya Raman at the table, or note it when you book with Mateo Rossi at table@shokutaku.example or on +31 10 555 0142. The drinks are made in the house for the menu of that week, so they follow the Tuesday vegetables and the fruit in the same way the pear tart does. Lunch guests and dinner guests may both ask. A children's plate at €14 is for guests under 12 and does not include a wine pairing.

A drink for a child can be requested at the table. The published prices stay as they are: lunch €26 or €32, dinner €58 or €78, pairing €38, children's plate €14. The request for a house-made drink adds none of its own. Tell us with the booking if the whole table wants the drinks in place of wine, especially for a private dinner.

VISIT

Visit and contact

Shokutaku Dining is at Havenstraat 41, 3024 Rotterdam, the Netherlands. Lunch is Tuesday to Friday, and dinner is Tuesday to Saturday.

Havenstraat 41

Tram 8 stops at Havenstraat, and the walk from that stop is three minutes. The entrance is step-free, and there is an accessible toilet. A plain link on this page will open the address in your own maps. The dining room seats 40: 32 at tables and 8 at the counter, around an open kitchen.

The private room is in the same building and seats 12, with a minimum of 8, for groups of 7 to 12. If you are nearby when a service starts, you may ask for a counter seat. A booked table is held for 15 minutes. Shokutaku Dining has been at this address since 2014, when Elena Vasquez and Tomasz Nowak opened in the former bakery.

posts.title: The Tuesday crates
posts.excerpt: Every Tuesday the vegetable crates arrive at the back door, and Elena Vasquez writes that week's menu from what they hold.
posts.content:
The back door on Havenstraat is the busy one on Tuesday morning. Polder Vegetable Co-op unloads crates of vegetables while the dining room is still empty. Elena Vasquez is already in the kitchen, in her stone apron, with the steel pass clear from the night before. The crates come inside before any list is written. That order is the whole idea of the menu.

Shokutaku Dining opened in 2014 in a former bakery at Havenstraat 41, 3024 Rotterdam. Elena and Tomasz Nowak kept the room at forty seats: thirty-two at the oak tables and eight at the counter, with the kitchen open in the middle. The private room, when a group has booked it, is a further twelve at one long table, and it eats the same dinner. Nobody in the building is served a vegetable that took a different route from the crate on the step.

Elena unpacks before she writes. Roots go into a bowl. Greens are looked over. What will not hold on a plate is kept for the stock. The spring vegetable starter, on the weeks it is offered, is built tall on a stoneware plate from whatever is firmest that morning. The greens that later sit beside the roast fish wait, because the fish is not a Tuesday delivery. Harbour Day Boats lands fish on Wednesday and Friday. Tuesday belongs to the co-op, and the first service to cook the new list is lunch the same day.

Jonas Berg is often at the floured bench while the crates are still coming in. His flour is not in them. Molen Ten Wind sends stone-milled flour on its own weekly delivery, and he shapes the loaves at dawn for the bread that will be on every table. If the co-op has brought fruit that will bake, the pear tart with cream becomes the sweet course. In other weeks the tart simply stays off the list, and the meal ends with hard cheese and oat crackers, or with whatever the pass can finish from the crates that are actually there. He does not send out for a different fruit to keep a dessert in place.

By late morning the list is short enough for the floor to learn. Lunch is Tuesday to Friday, 11:30 to 14:30, last order at 13:45, about seventy-five minutes. Two courses are €26. Three courses are €32. Lea Fischer runs that service. The first guests to eat the new vegetables are the lunch tables, and anyone who has asked for a counter seat on the way past. Dinner the same night uses the same crates. The dinner menu is four courses at €58. The kitchen tasting is six courses at €78. Both have a vegetarian version at the same price, which is a natural way to cook when the week has been written from vegetables before anything else is added.

Priya Raman tastes the first plates while she sets the wine. Six wines are poured by the glass, each named by grape and region and by nothing further. She pairs them with the food on the pass, not with a card from a previous month. A guest who wants four glasses with the dinner menu takes the pairing at €38. A guest who wants house-made drinks without alcohol asks for them with each course, and that request has no price of its own. Allergens are handled in the same plain way: noted on request, from the list Elena has just written, before the first plate leaves the pass.

Amara Mensah sets the mise en place from the same crates. Herbs are picked into bowls on the steel bench. White plates are stacked where Elena plates. The delivery is not announced as a special occasion. The whole menu is the delivery, so there is nothing beside it to single out. When the doors open, Tomasz seats the room. Mateo Rossi has already sent the confirmations. The crates in the alley are empty.

The rest of the week follows that Tuesday writing. Wednesday and Friday add the fish, roasted, with white beans and greens. Thursday and Saturday stay with the vegetables, the bread, and the rest of the list. Sunday and Monday the restaurant is closed, and the pass stays dark until the next delivery. Tables open thirty days ahead. A table is held for fifteen minutes. Please cancel at least twenty-four hours ahead by phone on +31 10 555 0142 or by email at table@shokutaku.example. There is no deposit. Groups of seven to twelve are booked into the private room, where the long table will be served whatever the crates decided, at the same €58 or €78 per guest.

People often ask Mateo for the menu in advance. He can send the shape of it: how many courses, the prices in euros, the hours, the choice of pairing. The specific plates wait for Tuesday, because that is when the kitchen knows them too. A booking for weekday lunch, or for any dinner through Saturday, is a booking for that week's crates as much as for a chair. Come for a short list, cooked at the pass, and expect it to taste like what was unloaded at the back door.

posts.title: Bread at six
posts.excerpt: Jonas Berg shapes loaves on a floured bench at dawn. The flour is stone-milled and arrives weekly from Molen Ten Wind.
posts.content:
Jonas Berg starts at six, when the room is still empty. He shapes the loaves by hand on a floured bench and leaves them to prove while the kitchen wakes up.

The flour is stone-milled and arrives weekly from Molen Ten Wind. The bread goes to the tables at lunch and dinner, and the sourdough is torn, not sliced.

Counter seats are the best place to watch the baking and the plating. Eight seats sit along the pass, and walk-ins may ask for a free one.

posts.title: Pouring by the glass
posts.excerpt: Priya Raman pours white wine by the glass. The four-glass pairing with the dinner menu is €38.
posts.content:
Priya Raman looks after wine and drinks. The by-the-glass list names the grape and the region and nothing more, so the conversation happens at the table.

The wine pairing is four glasses with the dinner menu and costs €38. Her list also holds house-made non-alcoholic drinks, served with each course on request.

The dinner menu is €58 for four courses. The kitchen tasting is six courses for €78.

posts.title: A long table for twelve
posts.excerpt: The private room holds twelve guests around one oak table. Groups of seven to twelve book it through Mateo Rossi.
posts.content:
The private room seats twelve guests around a single long oak table, with a minimum of eight. Daylight comes from the window and the candles stay unlit until the evening.

Mateo Rossi handles reservations and private dining. The dinner menu is €58 per guest and the kitchen tasting is €78; the wine pairing is €38.

Enquire by email at table@shokutaku.example. There is no deposit, and we ask for cancellations at least 24 hours ahead.
